According to Mark Gurman's latest Power On newsletter, Apple is preparing to include up to 1.5TB of memory in its upcoming M7 Ultra chip. This would finally allow Apple Silicon to match the maximum memory configuration offered by the top-tier Intel Mac Pro back in 2019.

The amount of available memory in Apple Silicon Macs has long been a limitation, primarily because Apple solders the memory onto the same package as the processor—while this enables extremely high transfer speeds and is precisely what makes unified memory possible, it also means memory capacity is constrained by the size of the chipset.

However, according to Mark Gurman, Apple appears to finally be preparing to close that gap. The company is working on an M7 Ultra chip configuration equipped with 1.5TB of memory:

He also noted that, due to the ongoing memory shortage, the final product may not ship with 1.5TB of memory. Nevertheless, Apple's engineering design is indeed being carried out to support that capacity.

Earlier this year, Apple discontinued the 512GB version of the Mac Studio equipped with the M3 Ultra chip, and subsequently discontinued the 256GB version as well, leaving 96GB as the only memory option for the top-tier Mac Studio. If you purchase the M4 Max model, the maximum configurable memory is 128GB.

Apple will also launch its all-new M5 Ultra chip later this year, featuring up to 768GB of unified memory, setting a new record for Apple Silicon.

Based on Apple's current memory pricing (approximately $25 per additional 1GB of memory), upgrading from the base 128GB configuration to 1.5TB would likely cost over $35,000.
